@@ hillmen
This group of Common Men traditionally lives in the hills an highlands. Many have become settled farmers and herders an make up majority populations in many rural areas. Others rema pure and live in the foothills and mountain vales.

Endurance: They are superb mountaineers and handle toug terrain with little additional effort. Height: Men average 5'10"; women, 5'6". Lifespan: Short; about 50-80 years. Resistance: Normal. @@ ulture
Clothing & Decoration: Crude wool and hide tunics wi leggings. They also wear rough over-coats, short cloaks, an fur hats. The woolens are woven in bright plaids, the colo indicating the wearer’s family lines and clan. Ritual tattooin is widespread. Fears & Inabilities: Numerous superstitions, notably a fear Darkness centering around the spirits in the earth and plan (which come forth at night). Lifestyle: Hillmen are herders, hunters, and gatherers who live extended families and reside in villages and fortified cla holds. They use chariots. Extremely theatric, they are gifte poets, musicians, singers, and storytellers. Pugnacious, the often settle disputes by raiding, fighting, or even warring o one another (and of course others).

@@ intro
Marriage Pattern: Monogamous, but one must marry out the family. Political marriages common. Line traced thro the female. Religion: Superstitious rituals devoted to a complex groupind vengeful petty deities. Many are vaguely based on the Hillmd peculiar interpretations of the “True Gods.” Oral traditionsin crucial to the keeping of histories and law. Sacrifices widespread and the clergy are both revered and feared.
